decisions.reason: Because it builds directly on the firm’s established geospatial integration business and was given its own webpage, management is likely to justify the investment and visible commitment by keeping it on the market.

A building data digital twin service fits the firm’s push into emerging geospatial enterprise applications, so despite somewhat lower public commitment the growth market and prior development effort favor continuing it.

Although closer to an adjacent capability than a core classic GIS product, the firm’s integration-oriented strategy and sunk development costs make management more likely to retain this security service than to withdraw it quickly.

An open GIS application development framework is highly consistent with the firm’s open, extensible, standards-linked positioning, so escalation of commitment and strategic fit both point toward keeping it.

The firm publicly announced this new identity service as enabling seamless GeoIT integration, and that visible commitment together with its relevance for enterprise and public-sector deployments makes withdrawal unlikely in the next year.
